title: Source migration and proposed disk cleanup
instructions: The source files now live in ignored downloads. The downloader and compatibility checks are implemented; Git history removal and final checks are pending. Optional comments can steer this work and the next storage cleanup. No experiment evidence has been deleted.

evidence.label: First real download: part 1 page list
evidence.text:
Inputs — congressionalg7391unit_page_numbers.json from https://archive.org/download/congressionalg7391unit/congressionalg7391unit_page_numbers.json; original size 181545 bytes and a recorded SHA-256 checksum.

Expected output — restore exactly the original bytes into a separate test folder, as required by your request for repeatable downloads.

Actual output — downloaded_verified; 181545 bytes restored with the original SHA-256 checksum. All 15 local originals separately match current Internet Archive sizes and SHA-1 checksums and your backup by SHA-256.

Differences — none for this first restored file. The other 14 files have not been downloaded again. Their existing local copies have been checked. Migration and Git history removal are pending. No historical text has changed.

evidence.label: Local storage: measured size and next cleanup proposal
evidence.text:
Inputs — directory sizes measured on this working copy, excluding inspection of the protected performance work.

Expected output — explain the roughly 51 GB folder and plan a smaller working copy while preserving evidence, as you requested.

Actual output — about 48 GiB total, the same scale as 51 GB in decimal units. artifacts occupies about 21 GiB, tmp about 23 GiB, sources about 2.38 GiB, Git about 559 MiB before rewriting, and the Python environment about 442 MiB. Two historical run folders account for 17.5 GiB; static-audit outputs add 2.9 GiB. Proposed next step: check references and exact file checksums, make verified archives outside the working folder, test restoring them, then relocate only cold outputs whose consumers have been checked. Similar file names do not prove duplicate bytes. The protected performance area is excluded.

Differences — this explains where most space lives; it does not yet establish how much is safely recoverable. No cleanup deletion has occurred. No change to historical evidence, human answers, source bytes or model results is proposed. Backup removal and performance-work cleanup are outside this plan.
